name: Seychelles
headline: Seychelles: +5.8% growth in 2025, 0.3% inflation, debt 51% of GDP
sections: Seychelles is a $2.3 billion economy (2025), the world's 190th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +5.8% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $36K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 5.4% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 0.3% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 2.6% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 2.6% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%.
Gross government debt is 51% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 79% in 2020. The general government balance is −1.0% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −7.7% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 172% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 10.0% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 48% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 76.3 years (2024). Population: 122 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
